title: Sewage Sample Extraction of Total Nucleic Acid Using QIAamp Fast DNA Stool Mini Kit
author: Dilip Abraham
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.buz4nx8w
materials: Prepare fresh each day: Add PhHV and MS2 working solutions to InhibitEX buffer: prepare only enough for N+1 samples to be processed that day: 1 mL InhibitEX buffer + 1 µL PhHV+ 1 µL MS2 is needed per sample (e.g. For 10 samples 11 mL InhibitEX+ 11 µL PhHV+ 11 µL MS2), mix well. PhHV (Phocine Herpes Virus) is a double-stranded DNA virus and MS2 is a single stranded RNA virus.They are used as internal controls to ensure the DNA extraction and PCR worked properly. We add them to the DNA extraction buffers in a known quantity and if they are not detected in the final sample at a specific level, we know that either 1) some kind of problem occurred in DNA extraction or 2) there were inhibitors in the PCR. During analysis we might consider removing these samples or adjusting the results in some way to account for the inhibition.

If the beads have not been pre-aliquoted to empty tubes: Add : ~ 370 mg (one eppendorf tube capful) of Sigma beads to the aliquot of stool (or blank tube). Some bacterial cells and parasite cells are difficult to break open with just chemical lysis buffers. So, we also use mechanical lysis (using a physical thing – beads – to break open the cell).

steps.title: Prepare InhibitEX Buffer
steps.instruction: Ensure the InhibitEX Buffer is thoroughly mixed by shaking. If a precipitate is present, incubate at 37 °C - 70 °C for approximately 15 minutes or until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Resuspend Sewage Pellets
steps.instruction: Combine and resuspend all 6 skim milk pellets (or blanks) using the InhibitEX/PhHV/MS2 solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of InhibitEX/PhHV/MS2 solution to the first skim milk pellet in a 50 mL conical tube.
Resuspend the pellet using a 2 mL serological pipette tip.
Use the resulting suspension to resuspend the 2nd pellet and continue sequentially until all 6 pellets are suspended and combined.

steps.title: Perform Mechanical Lysis
steps.instruction: Subject the combined suspension to mechanical agitation and lysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the combined suspension into a 2 mL screw cap tube containing glass beads.
Vortex for 1 minute.
Bead beat at maximum speed for 2 to 3 minutes.

steps.title: Perform Thermal Lysis
steps.instruction: Heat the suspension to assist in the lysis of stable bacterial and parasite cells.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the suspension at 95 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Clarify Sample
steps.instruction: Separate the liquid fraction from the stool particles.

substeps.instruction: Vortex for 15 seconds.
Centrifuge at full speed (approximately 20,000 x g) for 1 minute.

steps.title: Digest Proteins
steps.instruction: Use Proteinase K to degrade proteins in the sample.

substeps.instruction: Pipet 25 µL Proteinase K into a new 2 mL microcentrifuge tube (snap caps acceptable).
Pipet 600 µL of the supernatant from the previous centrifugation step into the tube with Proteinase K, ensuring no solid material is transferred (centrifuge again if necessary).
Add 600 µL Buffer AL.
Vortex for 15 seconds to form a homogeneous solution.
Incubate at 70 °C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge briefly to remove drops from the tube lid.

steps.title: Precipitate Nucleic Acids
steps.instruction: Prepare the lysate for spin column binding using ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 µL of ethanol (96–100%) to the lysate.
Mix by vortexing.
Centrifuge briefly to remove drops from the tube lid.

steps.title: Bind DNA to Spin Column
steps.instruction: Pass the total lysate through the QIAamp spin column to bind the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Place a labeled QIAamp spin column in a 2 mL collection tube.
Carefully apply 600 µL of the lysate to the column without moistening the rim.
Centrifuge at full speed for 1 minute.
Discard the collection tube and filtrate, then place the column in a new 2 mL collection tube.
Repeat the application of 600 µL lysate and centrifugation until all lysate (~1800 µL total) has been processed.

steps.title: Wash Spin Column
steps.instruction: Remove residual impurities from the bound DNA using wash buffers.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL Buffer AW1 to the column, centrifuge at full speed for 1 minute, and discard the filtrate in a new collection tube.
Add 500 µL Buffer AW2 to the column, centrifuge at full speed for 3 minutes, and discard the filtrate in a new collection tube.
Place the column in a final new 2 mL collection tube and centrifuge at full speed for 3 minutes to eliminate Buffer AW2 carryover.

steps.title: Elute Total Nucleic Acid
steps.instruction: Recover the TNA from the membrane into a clean tube.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the spin column into a labeled microcentrifuge tube.
Pipet 200 µL Buffer ATE directly onto the membrane.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 to 3 minutes.
Centrifuge at full speed for 1 minute to elute the TNA.
Save the filtrate (TNA) and discard the column.

steps.title: Store Extracted TNA
steps.instruction: Aliquot and freeze the extracted nucleic acids.

substeps.instruction: Pipet 100 µL of the extracted TNA into each of two storage tubes.
Store at -70 °C to -80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare MS2/PhHV Control Mix
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the extrinsic controls for extraction and amplification efficiency.

substeps.instruction: Quickly spin the tube containing lyophilized MS2/PhHV mix (stored at -80 °C) to bring the pellet to the bottom.
Add 50 µL STD diluent (stored at -80 °C) to each vial and mix well.
Use 1 µL per sample extraction following the SOP.
Store leftover mix at -80 °C; do not use if frozen-thawed more than twice.
